concept_en: How Knights and Bishops Complement Each Other
question_cn: 为什么马和象在开局中常常形成互补？
question_en: Why do knights and bishops often complement each other in the opening?

options.text_cn: 马和象价值相同，所以可以互换
options.text_en: Knights and bishops have equal value, so they are interchangeable.

options.text_cn: 马擅长控制固定格子（跳跃不受兵阻），象擅长覆盖长斜线；马强于封闭局，象强于开放局，两者覆盖对方的弱点
options.text_en: Knights jump over blockages and excel in closed positions, while bishops control long diagonals and thrive in open positions; each can cover the other's limitations.

options.text_cn: 马和象互补是因为颜色不同（一深一浅）
options.text_en: They complement each other because they are on different colors.

options.text_cn: 马和象没有本质区别，都是轻子
options.text_en: There is no meaningful difference; both are minor pieces.

explanation_cn: 马和象各有所长：马可以跳跃，不受兵阻，在封闭局面中表现出色，能占据对方难以攻击的强格；象控制整条斜线，在开放局面中射程远、威力大。两者互补意味着：马覆盖象管不到的格子，象覆盖马跳不到的远距离斜线。西班牙开局的Bb5就是通过「钉马」破坏这种互补关系。
explanation_en: Knights can jump over pawns and excel in closed positions, occupying strong squares that are hard to challenge. Bishops control long diagonals and are powerful in open positions. They complement one another because the knight covers squares the bishop cannot reach, while the bishop controls distant diagonals beyond the knight's range. In the Ruy Lopez, Bb5 can disrupt this balance by pinning the knight.
